title: WWT Partners Weekly Briefing
description: Cisco, Dell, HPE, NetApp, F5, Intel, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks, AWS, Google Cloud and VMware.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 2–9. New: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 8 that Nvidia's board opened an independent review after Jensen Huang's letter about an affair with a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy, and reported Nov. 7 that three House chairs asked him for a closed-door meeting. No Red Hat, IBM, Cisco, Dell, HPE, NetApp, Microsoft, Palo Alto, AWS, or Google Cloud newsroom item dated Nov. 6–9 was opened. No new Army or Department of War enterprise agreement was found. F5 and VMware were quiet; Intel's Nov. 3 process-kit note remains. The Amsterdam protest at a Microsoft data-center site is on the data-center page. Weekly cleanup removed the Cisco Model Foundry note, the RTX Spark laptop note, the Palo Alto PHP and Brotli advisories, the VMware ESX KEV item, and the AWS ML-KEM note.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: AMD's fourth-quarter guide would put it ahead of Intel
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 4 that AMD expects about $17 billion of fourth-quarter revenue, plus or minus 3 percent, against an Intel range of $15 billion to $16 billion, which Tom's Hardware said would put AMD ahead of Intel for a quarter for the first time. It said third-quarter revenue was $13.377 billion and Data Center revenue was a record $8.55 billion, 64 percent of sales. Chief executive Lisa Su said server revenue is expected to double year over year in 2027 and that data center should be more than 80 percent of total revenue that year. Tom's Hardware said Embedded revenue rose 29 percent year over year to $1.11 billion, which AMD attributed in part to aerospace and defense, and that Client and Gaming is projected to contract more than 20 percent sequentially in the fourth quarter.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: Intel Foundry released the Intel 14A process kit, version 0.9
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 3 that Intel Foundry last week made its Intel 14A process design kit, version 0.9, available. Tom's Hardware said Intel describes the node as reaching the performance and yield maturity expected at this stage, with the results backed by silicon validation. It said Intel plans to release process design kit 1.0 in the first quarter of 2027, which Intel says will validate readiness for high-volume manufacturing.

items.headline: OpenAI says Cisco is using GPT-6 Astra and Daybreak to speed network defense
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 3 that Cisco is combining network telemetry with OpenAI models, and that OpenAI's zero-data-retention terms let Cisco deploy the models on mission-critical systems. Jeetu Patel, Cisco's president and chief product officer, told OpenAI that controls can sit in front of every microservice, Kubernetes container, and cluster, and that two signals that look benign alone can show a pattern together. Patel said Daybreak and GPT-6 Astra have been what he called step-function improvements for Cisco's security posture and its customers', and that the tools can fit into existing scanning workflows. OpenAI said that through the Daybreak Defense Network the companies are exploring how security teams can triage exposure faster and enforce controls in Cisco Cloud Control.

items.headline: Palo Alto releases Cortex Cloud 2.3 with a cloud sensor and coding-agent integrations
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks said Nov. 2 that Cortex Cloud 2.3 adds Security Initiatives for tracking remediation goals, Cortex Cloud SaaS Security for 100 SaaS applications, and a Cortex Cloud Sensor for Linux cloud workloads and Kubernetes that it says uses up to 75 percent fewer resources. Palo Alto said the release connects security context and code scanning to AI coding agents through an MCP server, with native integrations for Claude Code and Cursor. It also said Unit 42 research showed an AI-assisted attack could reach data exfiltration in 25 minutes in a simulated scenario. The post says the release adds a supply-chain dashboard and artifact attestation, plus visibility for AI agents on AWS Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon SageMaker, and Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

items.headline: Dell says PowerScale OneFS 9.16 supports 500 tenants on one cluster
items.summary: Dell said Nov. 3 that PowerScale OneFS 9.16, which it calls a storage engine in the Dell AI Data Platform, supports up to 500 tenants on a single cluster, ten times the previous 50-zone ceiling. Dell said Access Zone-aware snapshots and quotas, shared network pools, object-ownership policies, and source-IP routing are meant to keep tenant boundaries in place on shared infrastructure. It said the release adds offline licensing registration, pAPI request rate limiting, and RPC-over-TLS for NFS traffic without a Kerberos deployment. Dell also said OneFS 9.16 adds S3 bucket ownership modes, including ObjectWriter, BucketOwnerEnforced, and BucketOwnerPreferred.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: Nvidia's board opens a review after Huang's letter about an alleged spy
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 8 that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang admitted, in a letter to staff, to an affair with a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy, and that the board said late Sunday it has no reason to believe sensitive corporate information or U.S. national security was compromised. The board said a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, will examine the available information, and that Huang supports the review. Tom's Hardware reported that Nvidia rejected suggestions of improper dealings, saying Huang regularly meets thousands of customers and that those interactions do not involve sensitive corporate information or national security secrets, and that Chinese officials dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded. Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 7 that Reps. John Moolenaar, Brian Mast, and Rick Crawford, chairs of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence, asked Huang for a closed-door meeting, citing reports that Megaspeed executive Alice Huang is a Chinese asset.
